---
name: bpm-scripts-generator
description: Generates the resources required to run a BPM process on IM-BPM for Accel Platform (screens, function containers, DDL/SQL, routing configuration, tenant setup materials, and where applicable batch, IM-LogicDesigner, and IM-Workflow materials), based on the specification documents created by bpm-docs-generator (specification.md, <feature name>-screen.md, <feature name>-logic.md, etc.). Use when the user mentions "create the necessary resources based on the BPM specification", "create the scripts based on the specification", "build the program from the specification", "turn the BPMN specification into an implementation", or "generate the screens and APIs for the BPM process". To newly create the specification documents themselves, use bpm-docs-generator. For the follow-up work of reflecting the screens and routing information generated by this skill into the formKey and similar attributes of the BPMN-XML, use bpm-xml-reflector. To incorporate the BPMN file itself into the tenant setup, use bpm-tenant-setup-generator.
---

# BPMS Resource Generation Skill

## Purpose
A skill set for generating the resources required for BPMS-ification from a specification document.
Resources are generated using the intra-mart Accel Platform script development model (JSSP).
It basically follows the guidelines of jssp-page-generator, but also documents IM-BPM-specific elements for scratch-screen integration.

## Referenced Skills

Resources are generated with reference to the following skill sets. For IM-BPM for Accel Platform-specific implementation conditions, see "Reference" and "Notes on IM-BPM Resources" below.

| Skill | Handling |
|---------|------|
| `.github/skills/jssp-page-generator/SKILL.md` + `.github/skills/jssp-imds-theme/SKILL.md` | 🟢 **Required reading** — covers the screen definitions and logic definitions in the specification |
| `.github/skills/jssp-localize-support/SKILL.md` | Required reading when there is a request for localization |
| `.github/skills/jssp-im-job-generator/SKILL.md` | Required reading when the specification uses a job (*1 may not be installed) |
| `.github/skills/jssp-tenant-setup-generator/SKILL.md` | Required reading when generating tenant setup materials such as the DDL and sample DML for the business data, the role/authorization materials, and the Importer configuration XML |
| `.github/skills/jssp-im-logic-generator/SKILL.md` | Used when the BPMN has a serviceTask with `activiti:type="logicdesigner"` and the `<BPM process name>-prompt` clearly describes the LogicDesigner specification — confirm with the user whether generation is needed before use |
| `.github/skills/base-im-workflow-generator/SKILL.md` / `.github/skills/jssp-im-workflow-usage/SKILL.md` | Used when the BPMN has a serviceTask with `activiti:type="applyworkflow"` or `activiti:type="draftworkflow"` and the `<BPM process name>-prompt` clearly describes the workflow specification — confirm with the user whether generation is needed before use |
| `.github/skills/bpm-tenant-setup-generator/SKILL.md` | Used when incorporating the BPMN file into the tenant setup |

*1 `jssp-im-job-generator` is one of the optional skills bundled with the intra-mart Accel Platform project template, and depending on the choices made when the project was created it may not be installed in this project. Confirm that `.github/skills/jssp-im-job-generator/SKILL.md` exists before referencing it. If it does not exist, do not fill in job-scheduler-specific implementation from memory or guesswork; instead, inform the user that the skill is not installed and confirm whether the batch materials should be generated and how to proceed (wait for the skill to be installed, exclude it from the current scope, etc.).

## Reference

Do not rely on memory or guesswork for IM-BPM for Accel Platform-specific implementation conditions — always read and confirm them against the following reference files.

| File | Content | When to reference |
|---------|------|----------------|
| `.github/skills/bpm-scripts-generator/reference/guide-bpm-form.md` | Sample code for request-type determination, permission checks, business data retrieval, mode determination, and screen display control | 🟢 **Required reading** — when implementing a screen (presentation page / function container screen processing) |
| `.github/skills/bpm-scripts-generator/reference/guide-bpm-api.md` | BPM API call patterns such as process instance start processing and task completion processing | 🟢 **Required reading** — when implementing process-integration processing (processing tied to a start event / user task) in a function container |

**Note when delegating to sub-agents:**
When delegating work to the screen agent or API agent, the orchestrator's prompt must explicitly state the **concrete paths** of the above reference files. Because sub-agents are launched with a fresh context, merely stating the skill name will not make them aware that the reference files exist.

## When to Use

When the user makes a request such as:
- "Create the necessary resources based on the BPM specification"
- "Create scripts based on the specification"
- "Create programs from the specification"

For the above requests, treat not only the JSSP materials but also the tenant setup materials as generation targets when the specification contains business data definitions or role/authorization definitions.

## Confirmation Flow Before and After Starting Generation

Before starting script generation, follow the procedure below (steps 1–6) to finalize the planned deliverables, whether optional materials are needed, and the policy for handling existing deliverables, and perform script generation **only after obtaining the user's explicit approval in the final confirmation of step 4**.

### 1. List the Planned Deliverables

Read the specification (under `<BPM process name>-prompt`, created by `.github/skills/bpm-docs-generator/SKILL.md`) and the original BPMN, then present the user with a list of the files and materials to be generated, organized by category.

**Basis for enumeration (primary source per category)**

Refer to the primary source below for each category and enumerate **only what is described there**. Do not infer items from the BPMN to fill in what the primary source does not contain.

| Category | Primary source |
|------|---------|
| DDL / SQL (table definitions, SQL templates; the 2WaySQL that the function containers call at runtime, placed under `src/main/jssp/src/<function name>/sql/`) | The business data definitions in `business-data.md` |
| Tenant setup materials (DDL, sample DML; for loading via the Importer, placed under `src/main/storage/system/products/import/basic/<key>/<version>/`) | The business data definitions in `business-data.md` |
| Tenant setup materials (roles, authorization) | The actor/role definitions in `specification.md`, the authorization URI declarations in the routing configuration of the screens/APIs, and the supplementary specification in `-prompt` |
| Importer configuration XML | The tenant setup materials above and the results of the interview conducted by `jssp-tenant-setup-generator` |
| Screens (presentation pages + function containers) | The "screen list" in `<function directory>/<function name>-screen.md` |
| API (function containers) | `<function directory>/<function name>-logic.md`, and the process details in `specification.md` |
| Batch (target of `.github/skills/jssp-im-job-generator/SKILL.md`, if applicable; *1 may not be installed) | The job descriptions in `specification.md` / `-logic.md` |
| Routing / tenant configuration | The screens and APIs finalized above |
| **(If applicable) IM-LogicDesigner materials** (e.g. `flow_definition.json` generated by `.github/skills/jssp-im-logic-generator/SKILL.md`) | The determination result of step 2 |
| **(If applicable) IM-Workflow materials** (import XML from `.github/skills/base-im-workflow-generator/SKILL.md`, action processing / screens from `.github/skills/jssp-im-workflow-usage/SKILL.md`) | The determination result of step 2 |

**Screen enumeration rules (strict)**

- Derive screens **one-to-one** from the rows of the "screen list" in `<function name>-screen.md`. Never include a screen that is not in that list among the planned deliverables.
- **Never enumerate a screen solely on the basis that a `userTask` / `startEvent` exists in the BPMN.** A task in the BPMN may have no screen; the authoritative source for that determination is the "Screen" column of the process details in `specification.md` (which contains `-` when there is no screen).
- For each enumerated screen, **also state the path of the `-screen.md` that is its basis and the screen definition name**. A screen whose basis cannot be shown is excluded from enumeration.

### 2. Determination and Confirmation of Generation Targets

#### 2-1. Materials that require both the BPMN tag and the specification description (screens / LogicDesigner materials / workflow materials)

The materials below are treated as generation targets **only when both** the BPMN tag and the specification description in `-prompt` are present. If either is missing, do not generate that material. No criteria are defined for judging whether "the specification is clearly described" — the agent responsible for generation judges this by reading the content of `-prompt` and determining whether it is concrete enough to start implementation.

| Material | BPMN-side condition | Specification-side condition | Behavior when both are met |
|------|------------------|-------------------|---------------------|
| Screens | The target `userTask` or `startEvent` exists | `<function directory>/<function name>-screen.md` contains the definition of that screen (screen items, validation, action processing), and the "Screen" column for that task in the process details of `specification.md` is not `-` | Include it in the generation targets (no per-screen confirmation is needed; present them together in step 4) |
| LogicDesigner materials | A `<bpmn:serviceTask activiti:type="logicdesigner">` exists | The `<BPM process name>-prompt` clearly describes the LogicDesigner specification (processing content, input/output, etc.) | Confirm whether to generate using `.github/skills/jssp-im-logic-generator/SKILL.md` |
| Workflow materials | A `<bpmn:serviceTask activiti:type="applyworkflow">` or `<bpmn:serviceTask activiti:type="draftworkflow">` exists | The `<BPM process name>-prompt` clearly describes the workflow specification (route structure, approvers, etc.) | Confirm whether to generate using `.github/skills/base-im-workflow-generator/SKILL.md` / `.github/skills/jssp-im-workflow-usage/SKILL.md` |

**Handling of the determination result (2-1: screens):**
- Generate only the screens that satisfy both conditions.
- **When the BPMN has the task but `-screen.md` has no screen definition, never generate a screen by inference.** This prohibition includes filling in screen items, validation, button processing, and layout from outside the specification.
- Treat a task with no screen definition as "no screen," and briefly report to the user within the conversation that it was excluded from the generation targets, along with the name of the task. There is no need to record this in a file.
- If the user needs a screen for that task, guide them to go back to `.github/skills/bpm-docs-generator/SKILL.md`, create the `-screen.md`, and then re-run this skill. Do not author screen definitions within this skill.

**Handling of the determination result (2-1: LogicDesigner / Workflow):**
- Confirm individually, "Shall I generate XX?" only for materials that satisfy both conditions.
- Keep materials whose implementation was approved in the generation targets, and exclude materials the user declined from the generation targets (the excluded ones are also removed from subsequent lists and completion reports).
- **When the BPMN has the tag but the specification description in `-prompt` is unclear or insufficient, and when the specification exists but there is no corresponding BPMN tag, do not perform the confirmation and do not generate materials using the generator.** There is no need to record the determination result or reason in a file — a brief report to the user within the conversation is sufficient.

#### 2-2. Materials whose determination does not depend on the presence of a BPMN tag (tenant setup materials / Importer configuration XML)

For the materials below, determine the generation targets mechanically from only the primary source listed in each row, regardless of whether tags such as role assignments are reflected in the BPMN. **The "only when both are present" rule of 2-1 does not apply to these materials.**

| Material | Primary source used to determine it is a generation target | Items to be finalized from the specification | Behavior |
|------|--------------------------|----------------------|------|
| Tenant setup materials (DDL, sample DML) | `business-data.md` contains business table definitions | There are definitions from which the DDL can be generated, such as table names, column definitions, types, and required conditions | Include it in the generation targets (no individual confirmation is needed; present them together in step 4). Delegate to `jssp-tenant-setup-generator` and place them under `src/main/storage/system/products/import/basic/<key>/<version>/` |
| Tenant setup materials (roles, authorization) | The actor/role table in `specification.md` lists role IDs and role names, or the routing configuration of the screens/APIs declares `<authz uri="service://...">` | The role ID, display name, authorization resource, target subjects, and permitted actions can be finalized from the specification | Include it in the generation targets (no individual confirmation is needed; present them together in step 4). Do not exclude it even when the role assignment attributes (`candidateGroups`, etc.) are not yet reflected on the BPMN side. Delegate to `jssp-tenant-setup-generator` and place the role/authorization materials under `src/main/storage/system/products/import/basic/<key>/<version>/` |
| Importer configuration XML | Any of the DDL, roles, authorization, or sample DML is generated | `artifactId`, `version`, `configNumber`, and `key` are finalized | Include it in the generation targets (no individual confirmation is needed). Generate `src/main/conf/products/import/basic/<artifactId>/import-<artifactId>-config-<N>.xml` |

**Handling of the determination result (2-2: tenant setup materials / Importer configuration XML):**
- When `business-data.md` contains business table definitions, treat the DDL and sample DML as tenant setup materials and delegate them to `.github/skills/jssp-tenant-setup-generator/SKILL.md`.
- Place the DDL and sample DML to be loaded into the tenant setup under `src/main/storage/system/products/import/basic/<key>/<version>/`. Place the 2WaySQL that the function containers call at runtime under `src/main/jssp/src/<function name>/sql/`, and never confuse the two.
- When the actors/roles in `specification.md` and the authorization requirements of the screens/APIs (the authorization URIs in the routing configuration) can be finalized from the specification, delegate the role/authorization materials to the same `jssp-tenant-setup-generator`. **Never skip generation on the grounds that the role assignment attributes are not reflected on the BPMN side.**
- When any of the DDL, sample DML, roles, or authorization is generated, also include the Importer configuration XML in the generation targets. Generate it at `src/main/conf/products/import/basic/<artifactId>/import-<artifactId>-config-<N>.xml`.
- Before delegating, finalize `key`, `artifactId`, `version`, and `configNumber`. Do not automatically infer `configNumber` from the loading status of the existing tenant; confirm with the user whether this is an initial setup or an incremental addition. For details, follow `.github/skills/jssp-tenant-setup-generator/SKILL.md`.
- When incorporating the BPMN file itself into the Importer, determine it separately as a target of `.github/skills/bpm-tenant-setup-generator/SKILL.md` and delegate it to that skill after approval. Generating only the DDL, roles, authorization, and Importer configuration must never copy the BPMN file automatically.

### 3. Check Existing Deliverables

For the planned deliverables listed in step 1 (DDL/SQL, tenant setup materials, screens, API, batch, routing/tenant configuration, and LogicDesigner/Workflow materials if applicable), check for each category whether the corresponding actual files already exist.

- **Categories with existing deliverables (user response required):**
  - Confirm with the user: "May I apply the content of this BPMN as a diff to the existing XX (category name)?"
  - **If Yes:** Proceed with generation/delegation for that category as a diff application (when delegating to a sub-agent, explicitly convey that it is a diff-application target and the existing file path).
  - **If No:** Present an alternative that does not apply a diff (e.g. ① exclude the category from this generation, ② back up the existing file under a different name and generate anew, ③ some other user-specified policy), and finalize the alternative to adopt together with the user.
- **Categories with no existing deliverables:** Proceed as new generation as-is.
- If the presence of existing files varies by category, you may judge each category individually (e.g. DDL/SQL is new, screens are diff-applied, etc.).

### 4. Final Confirmation Before Starting Generation

Present the user once again with the content finalized in steps 1–3 (the final list of planned deliverables reflecting the adoption decisions for the optional materials and the policy for handling existing deliverables), and explicitly confirm, "May I start script generation with the above content?"

- **Until an explicit response from the user stating that you may proceed is received, you must not start material generation or delegation to any sub-agent whatsoever.** Assuming the content of the response at the point the list is presented and continuing the processing on your own judgment is prohibited.
- If there are instructions for corrections or additions, reflect those instructions, present the list again, and repeat this step until approval is obtained.
- This step must not be omitted even when the content of steps 1–3 contains no determination results for optional materials or existing deliverables at all (i.e. new generation only).

### 5. Confirming BPMN Reflection After Generation Is Complete

For start events and user tasks whose screens (presentation pages) have been generated and whose corresponding `routing-jssp-config` paths have been finalized, the `formKey` (routing path) is ready to be reflected into `doc/<BPM process name>-prompt/<BPM process name>.bpmn`. **Do not perform this reflection automatically; always carry it out only after confirming with the user.**

1. Present the list of reflection targets (the ids of the start events / user tasks and the file names and paths of the corresponding routing-jssp-config).
   - Start events and user tasks that were determined to have "no screen" in step 2 and for which no screen was generated are excluded from the targets.
   - In the case of a diff reflection into an existing BPMN (screens for which a diff-application policy was chosen in step 3), include in the list only the routing paths that were regenerated or changed.
2. Confirm: "May I reflect the formKey into the BPMN (the copied version) with the above content?"
   - **If Yes:** Delegate to `.github/skills/bpm-xml-reflector/SKILL.md` (reflection of generated script content: `reference/bpmn-scripts-reflector.md`). When delegating, explicitly convey the correspondences from 1. (because `bpm-xml-reflector` is launched with a fresh context, the determination results on this skill's side cannot be carried over).
   - **If No:** Do not perform the reflection, and complete this step with the generated deliverables only. Advise the user to run `bpm-xml-reflector` again if the reflection becomes necessary later.

### 6. Recording the Interaction History
- Record requests to the prompt and reports of generation results in `doc/<BPM process name>-prompt/interactive-log.md`. If `doc/<BPMプロセス名>-prompt/interactive-log.md` already has entries, append to it.
  - Record the instruction content requested by the user verbatim.
  - Record the responses to the instruction content verbatim as well.

## **Notes on IM-BPM Resources**
### **The process instance ID and task ID are obtained from the parameters of the function container's init function.**
```
  function init(request) {
    // Request from a start event
    request.processDefinitionId;
    // Historical reference request for a start event
    request.historicProcessInstanceId;
    // Request from a user task
    request.taskId;
    // Expected to be added to the request parameters when requesting from a user task
    request.processInstanceId;
    // Historical reference request for a task
    request.historicTaskId;
    ‥‥‥
  }
```
- For the detailed procedure and sample code for request-type determination, permission checks, and mode determination using the parameters above, see `.github/skills/bpm-scripts-generator/reference/guide-bpm-form.md` (this section is only an overview).

### **Relationship Between Business Data and Screens**
- Basic policy
  - When calling a business data registration screen from a start event or user task to register business data, insert is the basic approach.
- For a process where a start event and multiple user tasks are involved in the input/output of business data (**regardless of whether it is the same screen or a different screen**):
  - If the business data definition has a task ID (i.e. it is managed with a composite primary key of `process instance ID + task ID`), then in line with the basic policy, the registration screens for the start event and each user task **default to a method that inserts** business data.
    - A record is added to the business data for each start event / user task. Existing records are not UPDATEd.
    - Only when there is an **explicitly confirmed** request such as wanting to limit the number of records may a policy be adopted as an alternative in which the first registration screen inserts the business data and subsequent user tasks update it.
  - If the business data definition has no task ID, the first registration screen inserts the business data and subsequent user tasks update it.
    - At the time of initial registration (a start event or the first user task), a record is added to the business data, and subsequent user tasks update that record with the screen input data.
  - For screen displays other than the initial registration, retrieve and display the business data entered at the immediately preceding start event or user task.
    - If the business data definition has a task ID and uses the composite-primary-key method (insert method), the retrieval condition is `process instance ID` + **a process variable holding the task ID of the immediately preceding start event / user task** (for the process variable setting pattern, see `.github/skills/bpm-scripts-generator/reference/guide-bpm-api.md`; for naming/proposal policy, see `.github/skills/bpm-docs-generator/reference/guide-specification.md`).
    - To satisfy the above retrieval condition, **the completion processing (`bpm.TaskService#complete`) for each task under this composite-primary-key method must always set its own taskId as a process variable for subsequent tasks to reference** (see "[Composite-primary-key method is required in principle] When passing your own task ID to a subsequent task" in `.github/skills/bpm-scripts-generator/reference/guide-bpm-api.md`; a plain complete(taskId) must not be chosen). When delegating to separate screen and API agents, the orchestrator must explicitly convey the correspondence of "which task needs whose taskId" (because an agent implementing only the read-side processing on the subsequent task side cannot notice a missing write-side implementation on the preceding task side).
    - If the business data definition has no task ID, or uses the Update method, the retrieval condition is the primary key of the business data (carried over via a process variable, etc.).
  - When registering a new record using the insert method, register the immediately preceding retrieved content (the input values from the previous step) together with the current screen's input values as a single record, and set **the task ID of the current start event / user task itself** as the task ID of the new record (for the detailed implementation procedure, see "Business Data Retrieval" in `.github/skills/bpm-scripts-generator/reference/guide-bpm-form.md`).
